INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel,
Public Grievances, Law and Justice, having been authorized by the Committee to present the Report
on its behalf, do hereby present this Sixty-eighth Report on Action Taken by Government on the
recommendations/observations contained in the Sixty-eighth Report of the Committee on Demands for
Grants (2013-14) of the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.
2. The Sixtieth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel,
Public Grievances and Pensions was presented to Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha
on 2
nd May, 2013.

on the Sixtieth Report of the Committee on 27 th August, 2013. The Committee considered the draft
Report and adopted the same at its meeting held on 3 rd January, 2014.
4. For the facility of reference and convenience, the observations and recommendations of the
Committee have been printed in bold and italics letters in the body of the Report.

REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the Ministry of
Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions on the recommendations/observations of the Department-
related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice in its
60
th Report on the Demands for Grants (2013-14) of the Ministry. The Report was presented to Rajya
Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on the 3 rd May, 2013.
2. The Action Taken Replies have been received from the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances
and Pensions in respect of the recommendations contained in the above mentioned Report, vide, their
communication dated 27 th August, 2013. These replies have been categorised as follows :
Chapter–I : The recommendations/observations which have been accepted by the Ministry
i.e., in respect of paras 2.16, 2.22, 2.28, 2.31, 3.3., 3.7, 3.8, 3.10, 3.12, 3.18, 3.28, 3.30,
3.34, 3.35, 3.43, 3.53, 3.56, 3.58, 3.63, 3.70, 3.72, 3.74, 3.82, 3.85, 3.87, 3.89, 3.91, 4.9,
4.25, 4.29, 4.51, 4.59, 4.61, 4.71, 4.73 and 4.85 of the Report. The Committee is pleased to
note that the Ministry has accepted these recommendations.
Chapter–II : The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to
pursue in view of the replies given by the Ministry i.e., in respect of paras 3.24, 3.32, 3.37,
3.41, 3.67, 3.76, 3.78, 3.93, 4.7, 4.11, 4.15, 4.23, 4.27, 4.31, 4.44, 4.55, 4.63, 4.66, 4.68,
4.75 and 4.77 of the Report. The Committee is convinced with the explanations advanced by
the Ministry and does not wish to pursue them as of now.
Chapter–III : The recommendations/observations in respect of which Committee has not
accepted replies given by the Ministry i.e., with regard to paras 3.39, 3.49, 3.51, 4.5, 4.6,
4.13, 4.17, 4.19, 4.20, 4.33, 4.36, 4.38, 4.41, 4.42, 4.45, 4.48 and 4.83 of the Report. The
Committee expresses its concern for not accepting the recommendations of the Committee
dealt with in Chapter–III of this Report and desires that the Ministry should furnish logical
explanation in respect of these recommendations.
Chapter–IV : The recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the
Ministry have not been received i.e., with regard to paras 3.51, 3.31, 3.22, 3.35, 3.26, 3.23,
3.45, 4.57, 4.79 and 4.81 of the Report, the Committee observes that the Ministry has
furnished evasive or interim replies in response to these recommendations. The Committee
desires that the Ministry should furnish action taken notes in respect of the recommendations
dealt with in Chapter–IV of this report.
3. The recommendations/observations of the Committee in its 60
th Report, the ATRs furnished by
the Ministry and the Committee’s further recommendations/observations have been dealt with in the
succeeding Chapters.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH
HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE MINISTRY
Reduced allocation made to the Ministry
Recommendation/Observation
1. The Committee takes note of the shortfall in allocation of R45.34 crores on the Plan
side and R55.85 crores on the Non-Plan side, made to the Ministry. The Committee hopes that
such reduced allocation should not adversely affect the implementation of important schemes/
projects of the Ministry.
(Para 2.16)
Action Taken Reply
1.1 The allocation was reduced by the Ministry of Finance based on the pace of expenditure and
mandatory cut imposed by the Ministry of Finance to maintain economy in the expenditure under Plan
and Non-Plan side. However, this Ministry has noted the Committee’s observation and will make
utmost efforts to ensure that the reduced allocation will not affect the implementation of important
schemes/projects. The Ministry will keep in mind the recommendation of the Committee while
projecting funds at RE stage and will also ensure additional allocation to various schemes based on
the requirement/need basis by making re-appropriation from the schemes where funds were under-
utilized or projecting the requirement under Supplementary Demands for Grants so that the reduced
allocation is not adversely affecting the implementation of the schemes.
Committee’s further observation
1.2 The Committee takes note of the reply.

steps should be taken to ensure that proper periodic monitoring and evaluation are done by
the Ministry so that allocated funds are utilized for the desired objectives. The Committee also
emphasizes upon the need for prudent financial management and chalking out realistic plans.
(Para 2.22)
Action Taken Reply

schemes is being monitored every week in the Senior Officers Meeting under the Chairmanship of

2.2 The Committee takes note of the reply and hopes that the steps taken in this regard prove

Study on Social Accountability Mechanisms
Recommendation/observation
16. The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry is giving importance to Social
Accountability Mechanisms. In the present era of enhanced transparency in governance and

greater awareness in the  public about their entitlements and rights, social accountability has

Action Taken Reply
16.1 A study was initiated by the Department entitled “Social Accountability Mechanisms” which
would explore ways and means of enhancing the ability of citizens (especially the poor and marginalized)

16.2 Committee of Secretaries (CoS) considered mainstreaming the Social Accountability Tools in all

Rural Development furnished a detailed note on Social Accountability Measures under MGNREGA. The

India-Commonwealth Symposium on Public Service Excellence
Recommendation/Observation
18. The Committee recognizes this initiative of the Department
(Para 3.58)

9
Action Taken Reply
18.1 Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, Government of India, in
collaboration with Commonwealth Secretariat had proposed to institute an annual International Programme
“India-Commonwealth Symposium on Public Service Excellence”.
18.2 Ministry of External Affairs while being supportive of the idea of the DARPG for instituting
an annual Symposium on Public Service Excellence, expressed their view that there is no need to
restrict the symposium to members of the Commonwealth, as the bulk of that membership comprises
small States and whose experience of public administration would have limited value for India. MEA
had further advised that it would be appropriate to do so under the ‘India’ brand name and after
identifying relevant countries from all across the world, who may be able to contribute more
constructively to such an annual event.
18.3 In view of the given consideration, DARPG now proposes to institute an “ India-International
Symposium on Public Service Excellence ” which would be a global annual event with the aim to
promote professionalism and the visibility of public service across the globe by sharing experience in
public administration. The Symposium will also foster the spirit of excellence in Public Administration
and in doing so, to acknowledge recognize and disseminate the innovative and extraordinary achievements
and remarkable done by civil servants and public sector institutions in improving public service
governance and delivery, and the quality of life of citizens and communities. Around 48 countries
across the globe plus European Union, which could sponsor entries on the theme of their choice, have
been identified for participation in the programme.
18.4 The programme will be an annual event of three days and will be organized on 24, 25 and
26 November every year in New Delhi, including one day learning journey opportunity.
18.5 W ith the active support of Ministry of External Affairs, the set of countries identified for
participation in the programme and International Organizations viz., World Bank, Asian Development
Bank (ADB) , Department for International Development (DFID) , Food and Agriculture Organisation
(FAO), International Labour Organization (ILO), Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development
(OECD), United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), United Nations Public Administration
Network (UNPAN), United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (UNICEF) and World
Health Organisation (WHO), etc. will be invited to participate in the programme. The members from
the International Organizations would be invited as Observer to provide global or other insight and to
share the lessons learnt on the themes identified for the programme.
18.6 Necessary clearances from Ministry of External Affairs and Ministry of Home Affairs from
political angle and security angle are being obtained respectively followed by the approval of Cabinet
Secretary.
Committee’s further observation
18.7 The Committee takes note of the reply.

15. The Committee takes cognizance of the above deposition of the Director, CBI. In this
regard, the Committee strongly feels that a delinquent official/ personnel should be meted out
disciplinary action, irrespective of whether he is a deputationist or cadre personnel. The
argument, that punitive action is taken against cadre personnel, while a deputationist is
merely repatriated to his parent Department, in itself, is indicative that unequal working
conditions prevail in the organization for the departmental personnel vis-a-vis the deputationists.
The Committee does not see this as a healthy trend. In Committee’s view, the above
statement of Director, CBI reflects only the state of helplessness in relation to the situation
of manpower in the CBI which is not a desirable situation. The Committee also desires that
Cadre personnel/officers should be given a major role in policy making.
(Para 4.44)

25
Action Taken Reply
● It is submitted that CBI is even-handed and fair in taking action against delinquencies of
its officers, be it deputationists or direct recruits. The action against an officer is taken
after weighing the gravity of the allegations and the merit of evidence available for
substantiation of the impugned allegations. In such cases where the evidence is not
preponderant enough to substantiate the charges, the direct recruits are given non-
sensitive assignments for certain duration and deputationist are repatriated to in their
parent cadres, if need be, in the best interest of the organisation. The salient guiding
principle is always to maintain impeccable conduct , unexceptionable probity and integrity
in the Bureau. It would be appreciated that departmental action would not serve any
purpose where allegations relate to personal foibles or where evidence is exiguous. Only
where provable evidence is available, regular departmental action is taken.
● It is humbly requested that the Hon’ble committee may kindly note the context in which
Director, CBI has made his deposition. It may be appreciated that considering sensitivity
of assignments and need for maintenance of utmost integrity within CBI, whenever there
is a hint of doubtful integrity without sufficient actionable evidence in respect of any of
its officers, the Bureau warns and counsels such officers but where their conduct proves
refractory it is compelled to take prophylactic action. In such cases, while it is easy to
repatriate a deputationist, it is difficult to find a non-sensitive assignment within CBI to
park a departmental officer.
● At the cost of belabouring the point, it is once again reiterated that equity animates all
the policies and practices of CBI.

departmental officers and reduce dependence on deputation.

Vacancies in CBI
Recommendation/Observation
10. The Committee recognizes the difficulties faced by CBI in getting Officers/personnel on
deputation. However, the Committee had, on earlier occasions, in its 24
th, 38 th and 51 st Reports
recommended that if vacancies prevail due to non-availability of officers on deputation, these
may be filled up by taking recourse to direct recruitment or promotion. However, the
Committee is unhappy to note that not much has been done in this direction. The Committee
wishes to drive home the point that a premier investigating agency such as CBI should have
an independent and proficient departmental Cadre of its own, rather than being dependent on
the States and other Organisations to spare their officers/personnel for deputation in CBI.
(Para 4.36)
Action Taken Reply
● In accordance with the recommendations of various Parliamentary Committees, provisions
for direct recruitment have been incorporated in the new RRs to ensure that the Bureau
becomes not only more competent professionally but also to ensure improved career
progression of the departmental officers. Once the above recommendations are implemented
by way of notification of new RRs, CBI would have a solid backbone of directly
recruited officers.
● In pursuance with the committee’s observations that vacancies prevailing in CBI due to
non-availability of officers on deputation may be filled by taking recourse to direct
recruitment or promotion efforts are underway to fill all the vacancies in deputation quota
by conducting DPCs wherever sufficient number of officers is available in feeder grade.
Moreover, direct recruitment as per the proposed RRs is to be done only at the rank of
SIs which would be done through SSC.
● In line with the earlier submission of Director CBI before the Committee, it is stated that
an organisation like CBI has to maintain impeccable conduct, unexceptionable probity and

36
integrity in the Bureau. While CBI is even-handed and fair in taking action against
delinquencies of its officers, be it deputationists or direct recruits, in cases where
allegations relate to personal foibles or where evidence is exiguous or not preponderant
enough to substantiate the charges, it is easy to repatriate deputationists, while it is
difficult to find a non-sensitive assignment within CBI to park a departmental officer.
(Also refer reply to para 4.44)
Recommendation/Observation
11. The Committee fails to understand as to how the vacancy position can be expected to
improve by not resorting to direct recruitment at such levels.
(Para 4.38)

● In the proposed Recruitment Rules the direct recruitment of Sub Inspectors is being
enhanced from 50% to 70%.
● Similarly at the level of Dy. SP, the promotion quota under the RRs when notified would
be 80% vis-à-vis 40% as per existing RRs which would not only obviate need for

officers.

11.1 The Committee takes note of the Ministry’s reply that direct recruitment as per the proposed
Recruitment Rules is to be done only at the rank of SIs. The Committee is not pleased to note that
not much thought has been given to the concern expressed by the Committee regarding non-
resorting to direct recruitment at the level of Deputy Superintendent of Police. The Committee

strengthen the cadre of directly recruited officers in CBI.
Paras 4.41, 4.42 and 4.46
Recommendation/Observation
12. The Committee is unable to comprehend the reason for fixing such a high percentage
as the quota for deputation in the ranks from Constable to Joint Director. The Committee is
apprehensive that the policy of not opting for direct recruitment in the ranks of Constable and
Dy. SP would, in the long run, lead to a situation wherein CBI would be totally dependent on
other Departments/States for their personnel. Therefore, the Committee recommends that this
policy should be re-looked and the Committee may be apprised of the action taken in this
regard in the Ministry’s Action Taken Reply.
(Para 4.41)
Action Taken Reply
● In accordance with various recommendations of the Committee, the Department has
taken action to revise the Recruitment Rules. In the revised RRs no deputation has been
proposed at the level of Head Constable, Assistant Sub Inspector, Sub Inspector, Additional
Superintendent of Police and Senior Superintendent of Police.

37
● Also, there is reduced deputation at the level of Deputy Superintendent of Police and
Superintendent of Police. The table below gives deputation quota in CBI as per the
existing RRs and proposed RRs:
Rank Existing RRs Proposed RRs
JD 80% 80%
DIG 75% 75%
Sr. SP 0% No deputation
SP 60% 50%
ASP 10% No deputation
Dy. SP 50% 10%
Inspr. 50% 50%
SI 0% No deputation
ASI 25% No deputation
HC 20% No deputation
Const. 60% 100% Deputation/absorption
● As is evident from the table above, the deputation quota has been substantially decreased
in the proposed RRs and is high only in the senior supervisory ranks of DIG and above.
In the rank of SP, it is limited to 50% only.
● In the rank of Constables, the proposed RRs have provision for 100% by deputation/
absorption. This would mean that while intake of Constable in CBI will be only through
deputation mode, the eligible, efficient and deserving among them would be absorbed and
become permanently a part of CBI. It is only that direct recruitment of constables is being
dispensed with because it is a very long drawn, expensive and extensive exercise which
is neither pragmatic nor desirable for a small organization like CBI having a very small
sanctioned strength of Constabulary.
● Further, it is stressed that CBI not only deals with corruption cases, but a variety of
offences that include threat to national security, national economy, violation of human
rights and conventional crimes having interstate and international linkages. Due to this
diversity of cases that the Bureau handles, an eclectic mix of competent, efficient,
sedulous and sapient officers with rich and diverse experience at supervisory ranks is
required, not only to supervise investigation of intricate and sensitive cases but also to
handle their diverse ramifications. It is in this backdrop that the deputation quota at Senior
Executive ranks has been kept high.
● Moreover, officers coming from diverse background bring in fresh ideas and varied skill-
sets with them. The cross-breeding of these ideas with those of direct recruit officers
leads to enunciation of strategies and tactics that have proved immensely successful in
unravelling convoluted cases.
Moreover, when deputationists officers go back to their respective cadres, they take back the
best practices in CBI and rich experience of working in premier investigating agency of the country.
This experience can be used by the State Police to build their own capacity in investigation of
corruption or other cases leading to less demand for CBI investigation in many matters.

38
Recommendation/Observation

(Para 4.42)
Action Taken Reply
13.1 We have noted the observations of the Committee and as explained at para 4.41 above, the
Recruitment Rules are being revised to reduce dependence on the deputation at various levels, improve
the career progression of the Departmental Officers and to benefit from the experience of the
deputationists especially in the supervisory ranks.
Recommendation/Observation
14. Taking into account the above mentioned facts, the Committee strongly recommends
that sincere efforts should be made to ensure that the departmental personnel get adequate
promotional avenues and that their expertise and knowledge should be optimally utilized.
(Para 4.46)
Action Taken Reply
● In accordance with the recommendations of various Parliamentary Committees, provisions
for direct recruitment have been incorporated in the new RRs to ensure that the Bureau
becomes not only more competent professionally but also to ensure improved career
progression of the departmental officers. Once the above recommendations are implemented
by way of notification of new RRs, CBI would have a solid backbone of directly
recruited officers.
● Also, efforts are underway to fill all the vacancies in deputation quota by conducting
DPCs wherever sufficient number of officers is available in feeder grade. Moreover,
direct recruitment as per the proposed RRs is to be done only at the rank of SIs which
would be done through SSC.
Committee’s further observation
14.1 The Committee takes note of the evasive reply furnished by the Ministry. The Committee
had recommended that the policy of not opting for direct recruitment in the ranks of Constable
and Dy. SP should be relooked. However, the Ministry has not touched upon this aspect in its reply.
The Committee takes strong exception to such evasiveness and directs the Ministry to furnish, in
this regard, a cogent reply in its Action Taken Note.
14.2 Further, the Committee takes note of the Ministry’s reply for fixing high percentage as
quota for deputation in higher ranks. The Committee is of the opinion that the presence of cadre
officers in higher ranks is essential to render effective supervision of the lower ranks since they
are more familiar with and have better experience and exposure to the procedures and the
protocol involved in successful prosecution and investigation, as compared to the deputationists.
The Committee strongly feels that the cadre officers’ rising to higher posts would serve as a

39
motivating factor for them. Therefore, the Committee desires that the Ministry should re-consider
the high percentage prescribed as quota for deputation, especially from the level of DIG and
above.
Recommendation/Observation
15. Further, the Committee is disappointed to note that as reflected in the Annual Report
of CBI, deputationist officers in the rank of SP were directly promoted as DIG, whereas cadre
officers in the rank of SP were promoted as SSP only which is a lower rank. Should the
Committee derive that the departmental officer is placed at a disadvantageous position,
although he is having an obvious edge over the deputationist, in terms of 54 skill, experience
and expertise, owing to his continuous exposure to specialized investigation which is regularly
being done in CBI?
(Para 4.45)
Action Taken Reply
● Deputationist officers in CBI in the rank of SP are primarily from IPS whose promotions
are governed as per All India Service rules. The IPS SPs before being promoted as DIG
become SSP albeit only for a year. Similarly, the promotions of cadre officers of CBI are
governed by their RRs which are duly approved by the Government. Moreover, the non-
IPS SPs in CBI are not eligible for promotion while on deputation to CBI and get
promoted to their next ranks as per the rules governing their parent cadre.
15.1 Further, the rules governing promotions in various services including that in CBI are approved
by the DoPT and Ministry of Law which has to take a holistic view to ensure that there is inter-
service parity amongst kindred services.
Committee’s further observation
15.2 The Committee takes note of the different eligibility criteria existing for promotion of cadre
officers and deputationists in CBI. The Committee does not find this to be a desirable situation and
is apprehensive that such discrepancies could lower the morale of the cadre officers. Therefore, it
recommends that the Ministry should consider this anomaly, while amending the Recruitment
Rules.

Recommendation/Observation
16. The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in its 56
th Report that in the event
of enacting a fresh statute for CBI not found to be feasible, requisite amendments may be

16.1 The Group of Ministers (GoM) constituted by the Government to consider the matter

Cadre Strength of IAS
Recommendation/Observation
1. The Committee is unhappy to note the large number of vacancies prevailing in the IAS
Cadre. The Committee is convinced that civil servants form the crucial component in the
administration, both at the Centre and the States, as they are mainly responsible for the
framing and implementation of important and vital policies of Government. Hence, vacancies
in this cadre will certainly hamper administrative efficiency. The Committee takes note of the
Ministry’s reply that it is closely monitoring the progress of recruitment under the promotion
quota of IAS. The Committee desires that the Department should take an active role in this
regard to rectify the situation at the earliest.
(Para 3.15)
Action Taken Reply
1.1 Over the years the cadre strength of the IAS of the States/Joint Cadres has shown an
increasing trend resulting in the increase in total cadre strength in the past few years for the country
as a whole. There has been a lower intake of the Direct Recruit IAS Officer during the years 1996
to 2006. The increased intake of the Direct Recruit IAS Officers from 2007 onwards was not enough
to fill up the gap. However because of the big expansion in the strength of various cadres of IAS
and less recruitment during the period preceding years the gap in the cadre strength of IAS and actual
intake in the service has increased enormously.
1.2 As a measure to fill up the gap in the direct recruitment quota of the service, this department
has gradually increased in the annual intake to the service, which would be clear from the table given
below, which indicates the annual intake to the service during the last 15 years:–

4. CSE-2001 59
5. CSE-2002 70

42

1.3 It is relevant to add here that the Baswan committee, constituted for the purpose of giving a
report regarding various issues concerning the cadre management of Indian administrative service has
recommended that it would not be appropriate to increase the annual intake to the IAS beyond 180
because in future a larger intake will create cadre management problems. Further, while conveying
approval to this Department’s proposal of determination of 180 vacancies to be filled in IAS through
CSE-2013, Hon’ble Prime Minister has directed this Department to consider the issue of shortage of
IAS officers in the light of the following suggestions given by this Deptt.
(i) To have a far more strict and stringent process of cadre review and to allow only such
increases in cadre strength as are absolutely essential and limiting the increase to about
5% (in each 5 year cycle of cadre review); and
(ii) To de-cadre a large number of posts from the IAS in the commercial and economic
sectors which have become redundant due to liberalization.
1.4 Further, taking note of the Committee’s observations, this Department has made concerted
efforts to reduce the gap/shortages in Promotion quota during the last one year and as a result, the
deficit/gap in the promotion quota which stood at 47.75% as on 1.1.2012 has been reduced to 29.67%
as on 1.1.2013.
1.5 It may be appreciated that action relating to filling up promotion/selection quota vacancies
through convening meetings of the Selection Committee falls under the purview of the concerned State
Government as well as the UPSC. This Deptt.’s role is confined primarily to determination of
vacancies for a particular SL year. Shortage of IAS Officers in promotion quota is due to delay in
filling up vacancies on account of delay in conducting selection committee meetings, which can be
attributed due to various reasons, the primary one of which is the litigation regarding the seniority of
State Civil Service Officers.
1.6 However, recognizing the need to sensitize the State Governments and to monitor the progress
of recruitment in the Promotion Quota of IAS, meetings with the Principal Secretaries of the State
Governments would be convened twice during the year to pursue with the State Governments to speed
up/expedite the recruitment process.
Committee’s further observation
1.7 The Committee takes note of the factors elaborated upon by the Ministry, responsible for the
vacancies prevailing in the IAS Cadre. The Committee has noted that the deficit/gap in the

43
promotion quota which stood at 47.75% as on 1.1.2012 has been reduced to 29.67% as on 1.1.2013.
The Committee recommends that the DoPT should take effective steps to further reduce the deficit.
The Committee also desires that the DoPT should take a proactive role to ensure that the
recruitment process in the promotion quota of IAS is expedited.
Special Recruitment Drive
Recommendation/Observation
2. The Committee acknowledges the fact that the reservation policy in Government sector
is, in a way, instrumental in inclusive growth. The Committee strongly feels that the full
benefits of the policy would accrue to the deserving persons only if the policy is implemented
in its true letter and spirit, as per the constitutional mandate. Keeping in view this reality, the
Committee recommends that the Department should chalk out a multi-pronged strategy to
ensure that the reserved vacancies are given wide publicity in regional and vernacular
languages also and the capacity building measures are strengthened.
(Para 3.21)
Action Taken Reply
2.1 The instructions already exist that reserved vacancies are not only to be reported to the Local
Employment Exchange but also to other Employment Exchanges, in case sufficient number of reserved
candidates are not available from the Local Employment Exchanges. Instructions further provide to
announce reserved vacancies in the AIR Stations located in areas with concentration of SCs and STs
population. Further, instructions also exist to advertise vacancies in Employment News (which is
published in regional languages also) published by the Publication Division of the Ministry of
Information and Broadcasting. To further ensure that the SC/ST vacancies are widely circulated and
securing more candidates belonging to these categories, a list of SC and ST Organizations (State-wise)
have been identified and such reserved vacancies are also required to be reported to them.
Committee’s further observation
2.2 The Committee recognizes the fact that instructions regarding giving publicity and availability
of information about reserved vacancies already exist. However, the Committee is doubtful as to
whether the benefits of reservation have actually percolated to the beneficiaries. In this regard, the
Committee recommends that DoPT should take a proactive role and co-ordinate with the respective
Ministries/Departments/Agencies to ensure that the backlog of reserved vacancies is filled up.
Paras 3.2.2, 3.25 and 3.26
Recommendation/Observation
3. The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in its 56
th Report that the Department
of Personnel and Training should oversee, monitor, execute and implement the reservation
policy and should also prevail upon the various Central Recruiting Agencies and other concerned
Departments so that they take all possible steps to ensure that the backlog vacancies are filled
up without delay.
(Para 3.22)
Action Taken Reply
3.1 Under the Allocation of Business Rules, each Department/Ministry is to see whether instructions

44
on reservations are being implemented in true perspective. Often, the cases involving Scheduled Castes
and Scheduled Tribes are submitted to the Minister-in-charge for seeking his directions.
3.2 It is also submitted that as per the provisions of Transaction of Business Rules and Allocation
of Business Rules, all Departments/Ministries are equal and the Department of Personnel and Training
has no power of superintendence over other Ministries to monitor the implementation of reservation
policy. This is why each Ministry/Department is entrusted to monitor and implementation of reservation
policy in their Department/Ministry/Attached and Subordinate offices and organizations under their
administrative control. It is also submitted that grievance of SCs and STs are taken care of by the
Ministry/Department itself.
3.3 To ensure that the instructions on reservation are implemented properly, each Ministry/
Department has a liaison officer separately for SCs and STs. He is required to bring out any lapses/
shortcoming in implementation of orders on reservation directly to Secretary/Additional Secretary of
the Ministry/Department concerned.
3.4 Department of Personnel and Training has issued instructions from time to time that:
“If sufficient number of suitable SC/ST/OBC candidates do not become available to fill up the
vacancies reserved for them in the first attempt of recruitment, a second attempt should be
made for recruiting suitable candidates belonging to the concerned category in the same
recruitment year or as early as possible before the next recruitment year so that the backlog
reserved vacancies are not created. If, even after making such efforts, the reserved vacancies
are not filled and backlog reserved vacancies are carried forward to the subsequent recruitment
year, concerted efforts should be made to fill up the backlog reserved vacancies as soon as
possible”.
3.5 The Department of Personnel and Training have been launching Special Recruitment Drives to
fill up the backlog reservation vacancies of SCs and STs from time to time, in a time-framed manner.
The last such Drive was concluded in March, 2012 to fill up the backlog reserved vacancies of SCs,
STs and OBCs. As per information received from various Ministries/Department, there were 75,552
backlog reserved vacancies of SCs, STs and OBCs out of which 48,034 have been filled up.
Special Recruitment Drive for Persons with Disabilities
Recommendation/Observation
4. The Committee feels that the success rate of the Special Drive which is 39.78%, is
quite low.
(Para 3.25)
4.1 The Committee is disheartened to note that in spite of the existence of vacancies for
persons with disabilities and the availability of persons with good amount of skill and talent,
the vacancies continue to remain unfilled. The Committee would like to impress upon the
Ministry to give due thought and consideration to this situation and to come out with a definite
action plan to address this problem.
(Para 3.26)
Action Taken Reply
4.2 Achievement of the Special Recruitment Drive up to 30
th June, 2011 as reported by the
Ministries/Departments was submitted to the Cabinet through a Cabinet Note. The Cabinet in its
meeting held on 04.01.2012 considered the Cabinet Note and gave direction to complete the process
of filling up the backlog vacancies by 31
st March, 2012 by all Departments and also to institutionalize

45
a mechanism for enhancing the employability of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribe, Other Backward
Classes and differently abled persons after discussions among the Department of Personnel and
Training, Ministry of Tribal Affairs and the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
4.3 The achievement of the Drive concluded on 31.03.2012 was analyzed and the areas of concern
for less employability and measures to address the problems have been considered. The Cabinet has
been apprised of the achievement of the Special Recruitment Drive and related issues.
Committee’s further observation
4.4 The Committee desires that DoPT, apart from issuing necessary instructions, should
monitor their implementation periodically and take up with the concerned Ministries/Departments
the non-adherence thereof, if any, and take adequate rectifying action. The Committee also
recommends that DoPT may have a re-look at the strategy for launching Special Recruitment
Drives, in order to enhance its success percentage.
Special Recruitment Drive
Recommendation/Observation
5. In this regard, the Committee also feels that the DoPT should play a proactive role and
ensure the appointment of Liaison Officer in respect of matters relating to representation of
SCs and STs, in all Ministries/Departments, without any further delay. The Committee strongly

and STs in their respective Departments.
